messages:
maria.supp: Heads up — customer 'acme-marketing' reporting large p95/p99 increases since ~09:15 UTC. They see >5s queueing before requests hit workers and a fair number of 504s. @jon.oncall can you triage?

maria.supp: Repro from their side: steady traffic (100rps) -> sudden spike of medium-long prompts -> queue depth grows, many requests wait ~4-6s then timeout. Sample request_id: req_20260315_9A3F. Region: us-west2, model: gpt-mini-2Q.

jon.oncall: looking. grabbing traces and admission metrics now. do we have recent rollout/changes in admission_control? @lee.runtime any config changes?

lee.runtime: not deployed any config today. I'm pulling admission metrics and KV cache evictions. If queueing is at worker ingress might be concurrency overwhelm or a new workload pattern causing many long-lived streams.

arjun.eng: also check prefix cache hit rate — if cache miss causes longer generation per request we can see pileups. can we get a flamegraph?

maria.supp: customer attached logs:
```
2026-03-15T09:14:58Z WARN admission: request queued depth=42 wait_ms=4231 req=req_20260315_9A3F route=/v1/chat/completions
2026-03-15T09:14:58Z ERROR upstream: worker timeout after 6000ms
```

maria.supp: curl they used for repro:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-mini-2Q","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"long prompt ..."}], "max_tokens":1024}'
```

jon.oncall: pulling the span for req_20260315_9A3F... ok span shows: client -> edge -> admission -> router -> worker queue -> worker. router latency small, admission queue wait high ~4s, worker processing ~1.2s. Admission drop ratio increased around 09:12.

jon.oncall: immediate mitigation options:
- increase admission concurrency quota for that customer temporarily
- lower per-request timeout on the edge to fail fast and avoid worker backlog (short-term)
- enable fallback route to a smaller model for heavy customers

lee.runtime: can we flip a fast admission policy change? we have on-the-fly config:
```
# temporary admission override
admission_control:
  per_customer_max_concurrency: 8  # was 4
  queue_max_inflight: 500
  fallbacks:
    allow_smaller_model: true
```

lee.runtime: I can apply to the us-west2 admission tier now; it will increase burst capacity. note: will increase cost for route.

maria.supp: customer asked for a workaround while we triage. they can route a subset of traffic to a smaller model but want to minimize code changes.

arjun.eng: alternative quick patch: enable KV prefix caching for the hot prompt family to cut worker time in half. config snippet: `cache.prefix.enable=true` and add prompt hash to cache key. Might be lower risk than increasing concurrency.

jon.oncall: I'm enabling temporary per-customer concurrency bump for acme-marketing to 8 and enabling smaller-model fallback. I'll monitor QPS and p95.

infra-bot: deploy:admission-config-v2 started by jon.oncall at 2026-03-15T09:17:03Z :rocket:

jon.oncall: done. admission policy applied. early signs: queue depth dropped from 42 -> 10 within 30s, p95 reduced from 3.8s -> 1.1s. still watching for regressions. :eyes:

maria.supp: customer confirms fewer 504s, reporting improvement. they still see occasional spikes when they do bulk batch calls.

lee.runtime: next steps (recommended):
1) run targeted canary of KV prefix caching for that tenant for 30m.
2) add admission-slo alert for queue_wait_ms > 2000ms per-customer to trigger autoscale before timeouts.
3) investigate workload pattern to see if prompt lengths suddenly changed (maybe a campaign).

arjun.eng: logging note: capture sample prompt hashes (anonymized) + token counts per request to correlate. add to the debug trace pipeline for acme-marketing for 2 hours.

maria.supp: created internal ticket #SUP-3421 and cc'd acme contact. I'll schedule a post-mortem with customer and island root cause. thanks all. :pray:

jon.oncall: leaving monitoring on for 2hrs, will escalate to SRE if queue depth grows again.

lee.runtime: I'll prepare a small rolling restart plan for the admission tier if needed, and a permanent config suggestion: per-customer burst pools.

infra-bot: alert: admission_queue_wait > 2000ms for us-west2 for 1m — resolved automatically at 2026-03-15T09:20:30Z

maria.supp: marking thread resolved for now, will reopen if customer reports further slowdowns.
